decision_authority.policy: MRX continuous quality-gated publication and two-image article creative directive

title: Uncovering Hidden Costs: What Every Mineral Rights Seller Should Know Before the Review
findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is 980e9ffe2d862957155e1d82c529547627d6d8f5a179072816380ebc48e22578; all 6 declared sources passed live access review.

MRX claims remain bounded to its current FAQ, methodology, and terms; Texas recording law is expressly limited to a state-specific example; and IRS claims remain general disposition and basis concepts that require owner-specific professional review.

The article uses no fabricated owners, buyers, contracts, deeds, prices, acreage, ownership decimals, tax results, offers, testimonials, success rates, or owner-specific title, legal, tax, accounting, appraisal, investment, or transaction conclusions.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Frequently Asked Questions (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX FAQ states that the directional underwriter review is free, requires no payment card, creates no obligation to sell, is not a certified valuation, and may precede an MRX buyer relationship that is disclosed when applicable.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the FAQ only for MRX’s current review price and service boundaries and its provider-interest disclosure; it does not extend the free-review statement to outside work, promise a result, interpret an agreement, or recommend a transaction.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Published DCF Methodology (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX methodology separates a directional asset range from actual buyer offers and expected owner net, and requires dated inputs, assumptions, and limitations.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the methodology only to distinguish property evidence, a directional range, proposal consideration, adjustments or deductions, and expected owner net; it does not value a specific interest, establish legal rights, or predict a transaction result.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Terms of Use (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX terms state that website information is educational and not legal, tax, financial, investment, engineering, or certified appraisal advice.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the terms only to preserve educational and professional boundaries; it does not use them to interpret a buyer contract or determine an owner’s rights.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Legislature, Property Code Chapter 12, Recording of Instruments (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: Texas Property Code Chapter 12 provides a state-specific example of formal requirements associated with recording instruments concerning real or personal property.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses Chapter 12 only to show why recording-related duties and costs require document-specific review in a Texas transaction; it does not extend Texas law elsewhere or claim that recordability proves validity, title, authority, delivery, consideration, priority, or an owner-specific result.

sources_inspected.label: Internal Revenue Service, Publication 544, Sales and Other Dispositions of Assets (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: IRS Publication 544 explains that gain or loss on a sale or other disposition generally depends on the amount realized and adjusted basis, with treatment depending on the property and transaction facts.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the publication only to identify general federal disposition concepts and prompt an owner-specific tax handoff; it does not classify an owner’s asset or calculate basis, gain, loss, depletion, tax, withholding, or filing treatment.

sources_inspected.label: Internal Revenue Service, Publication 551, Basis of Assets (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: IRS Publication 551 explains general federal basis concepts and adjustments that can depend on acquisition history and the asset’s facts.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the publication only to identify basis as an owner-specific record and professional question; it does not determine basis, depletion, allocation, gain, loss, tax, withholding, or filing treatment.
